title: Keep Bun's lockfile as the only lockfile

facts.note: The repository/workspace is declared as using Bun as its package manager (workspace declaration), independent of which lockfiles currently exist. Lockfile presence alone is not proof of the package-manager choice (e.g. mid-migration repos).

Foreign lockfile basenames present anywhere in the declared, non-excluded scan roots of the Bun workspace (excluding node_modules, dist, build, _generated), regardless of version-control status (committed or not).
Lockfiles and package.json are recognisable by basename.

Diff-level observer needed to know a dependency was added/changed in package.json or a foreign lockfile was introduced in this change. The agent's intent to run a particular install command is not observable; only the resulting diff is.
Detector finding reported at line 1 of each foreign lockfile.
Task text mentioning dependency installation or package-manager migration. Text-based proxy only; there is no structured 'migrating to Bun' declaration.

fires: In a declared Bun workspace, any `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock` or `pnpm-lock.yaml`/`.yml` exists in a non-excluded scan root (committed or uncommitted).
In a declared Bun workspace, the current change adds or changes a dependency in a package manifest.
A repo declared as a Bun workspace while migrating to Bun still has its old lockfile present.
A monorepo package deliberately not on Bun has its own foreign lockfile inside the scanned tree of a Bun workspace.
doesNotFire: A vendored or fixture lockfile inside `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` or `_generated`.
A Bun workspace whose only lockfile is `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb` and whose current change adds or changes no dependency.
A repository not declared as a Bun workspace.

given: A declared Bun workspace (package manager chosen as Bun, independent of which lockfiles exist) with scan roots outside excluded trees
when: the tree holds a foreign lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`/`.yml`), committed or not, or the current change adds or changes a dependency
then: Keep Bun's lockfile as the single dependency-resolution source: remove npm, Yarn and pnpm lockfiles; none may sit alongside `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`.
prefer: During GREEN: if the current change adds a dependency, install it with Bun.
During GREEN: remove only foreign lockfiles; regenerate `bun.lock` only when dependency state actually changed; keep package-manager behavior otherwise untouched.
avoid: Keeping a second lockfile as a temporary convenience, including during a migration window.
Suppressing the finding for a monorepo package deliberately not on Bun; it stays reported until it moves to Bun or out of the scanned tree.
unless: A vendored or fixture lockfile inside an excluded tree (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) is never scanned.
why: Two lockfiles mean two resolvers disagree; whichever command a developer or CI runs wins, causing invisible drift and "works on my machine, breaks in CI". Risk peaks while migrating to Bun: the old lockfile is still committed, someone runs `npm install` out of habit, the trees fork, and a deploy fails much later.
evidence: The current behavioral acceptance and the install/check path pass.
No foreign lockfile basename exists in the declared scan roots; only Bun's lockfile governs dependency resolution.
verifier_detail: Foreign lockfile basenames: `package-lock.json` (npm), `yarn.lock` (Yarn), `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `pnpm-lock.yml` (pnpm) — resolution records written by a package manager that is not this stack's.

Detector is a zero-dependency Bun detector that walks the declared scan roots matching foreign lockfile BASENAMES and reports each at line 1 — the file itself is the fact, so there is no line to point at.

atdd-bun has no per-rule scope: a monorepo package deliberately NOT on Bun stays reported until it moves to Bun or out of the scanned tree; the finding is the stack decision's open item, not something to suppress.

Resolution drift: two lockfiles pin different versions of the same transitive dependency, so the installed tree depends on which tool ran last; it is invisible in review because nobody reads a lockfile diff.

Migration detail: a repo moving to Bun passes through a window where the old lockfile is still committed; that window is exactly when the graphs diverge (someone runs `npm install` out of habit, the trees fork, discovered much later in a failing deploy). The rule matters more during a migration than after one.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Bun-stack realization of the agnostic "dependency resolution has one source of truth" obligation.

Characterised as a "one lockfile" repo-hygiene obligation; the cheapest rule in the extension to satisfy and one of the most expensive to violate (failures cost hours per occurrence and are never attributed to their actual cause).

sharedNodes.text: Strict disposition: fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
